quick: 150 mg once daily; may increase to 300 mg once daily
Take consistently; avoid high-fat meals (reduce absorption)
Contraindicated - boxed warning for fetal toxicity/death
Avoid with ACEi/ARB if GFR <60; monitor K+ and creatinine
summary: Aliskiren is the first orally active direct renin inhibitor, used to treat hypertension alone or with other agents. The usual dose is 150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg if needed. It carries a boxed warning: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury and death, so it must be stopped when pregnancy is detected. It is contraindicated in combination with ACE inhibitors or ARBs in patients with diabetes because of increased renal impairment, hyperkalemia and hypotension.
indications: Treatment of hypertension in adults, alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

dosage.d: 150 mg once daily; if BP not controlled may increase to 300 mg once daily
dosage.n: Doses above 300 mg give no added BP reduction but more diarrhea

dosage.d: Add to other antihypertensives (e.g., thiazide, amlodipine) when monotherapy inadequate
dosage.n: Do NOT combine with ACEi/ARB in diabetics; avoid dual RAAS blockade

admin: Take by mouth once daily at the same time each day
Establish a routine pattern with regard to meals; high-fat meals substantially decrease absorption
Do not co-administer with high-fat foods
Discontinue as soon as possible when pregnancy is detected
Correct volume/salt depletion before starting to reduce symptomatic hypotension
moa: Aliskiren directly inhibits renin, the enzyme that catalyzes the rate-limiting first step of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system - conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I. By blocking renin at its point of activation, it reduces plasma renin activity and decreases formation of angiotensin I and angiotensin II, producing vasodilation and lowering blood pressure.

absolute: Pregnancy (boxed warning - fetal toxicity and death)
Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors or ARBs in patients with diabetes mellitus
Concomitant use with cyclosporine or itraconazole (potent P-gp inhibitors)
relative: Renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min) with concomitant ACEi/ARB
Concomitant potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements

preg: Contraindicated. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus, especially in the second and third trimesters (oligohydramnios, fetal renal failure, hypotension, skull hypoplasia, death). Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
lact: It is not known whether aliskiren is excreted in human milk; it is present in the milk of lactating rats. Because of potential for serious adverse reactions in the nursing infant, breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: Use with caution; monitor renal function periodically. Combination with an ACE inhibitor or ARB is contraindicated in diabetics and not recommended when GFR is below 60 mL/min because of increased risk of renal impairment, hyperkalemia and hypotension.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild to severe hepatic impairment.

major: ACE inhibitors / ARBs - dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia, hypotension and renal failure; contraindicated in diabetes
Cyclosporine - markedly increases aliskiren exposure; avoid
Itraconazole - markedly increases aliskiren exposure; avoid
moderate: NSAIDs - reduce antihypertensive effect and may worsen renal function in elderly/volume-depleted/renally impaired
Furosemide - aliskiren reduces furosemide exposure and effect
minor: Other antihypertensives - additive blood pressure lowering
interactions.food: High-fat meals substantially decrease absorption; take consistently with regard to food.
interactions.alcohol: May add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect; limit intake.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum potassium, creatinine, BUN and uric acid; increases plasma renin concentration while lowering plasma renin activity.

serious: Angioedema (face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, larynx)
rare: Elevated uric acid, gout, renal stones

monitoring: Blood pressure response and for symptomatic hypotension
Serum potassium periodically, especially with other RAAS agents or potassium-sparing drugs
counsel: Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant; this medicine can harm the unborn baby
Take it at about the same time each day and keep a consistent pattern with meals
Avoid taking it with high-fat meals as this reduces how much is absorbed
Report swelling of the face, lips, tongue or trouble breathing right away
Do not use salt substitutes containing potassium without checking with your doctor
pk: BP lowering within hours; full effect over ~2 weeks
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture
pearls: Boxed warning: stop immediately when pregnancy is detected - fetal toxicity/death
Contraindicated with ACEi/ARB in diabetics (ALTITUDE trial); avoid dual RAAS blockade generally
Diarrhea is dose-related and more common at 300 mg
High-fat meals markedly lower absorption - counsel on consistent dosing
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: The most likely manifestation is hypotension due to the antihypertensive effect. Treat with supportive care; place the patient supine and give intravenous fluids. Aliskiren is minimally dialyzable.
